transcript.text: Hi, my Hotpoint Aquarius dryer is taking forever to dry and the top gets really hot. Model is TCM580GUK if that helps

The most likely cause is restricted airflow: fluff in the filter, condenser/second filter, or a blocked vent path makes a dryer take much longer and can make its top unusually hot. A warm top can be normal, but “really hot” together with poor drying is a reason to deal with airflow before using it much more. 1. Switch it off and unplug it. Remove and clean the fluff filter in the door area. Clear lint from its surround as far as you can reach safely. A matted filter strongly supports an airflow problem.
2. Check the lower front flap. If there is a removable condenser or second filter, take it out and rinse fluff away under the tap; let it drain before refitting. If instead the dryer has a hose to an outside wall, check the hose is short, not crushed or kinked, and that the outside flap is clear.
3. For the next test, use a normal heat programme with a modest, well-spun load—no more than about two-thirds of the drum. Overloading or laundry coming in very wet can also make drying seem endless. If the filters and air path are clear but it still becomes excessively hot or drying remains poor, the next suspects are the blower fan or the temperature-control/overheat-protection parts, which are better checked by an engineer rather than replacing anything blindly. If there is any burning smell, smoke, scorching, or it cuts out hot, stop using it and leave it unplugged until inspected.

Thank you. I unplugged it and the door filter had a thick layer of fluff on it, which I'll admit I sometimes forget to clean. The condenser at the front bottom had lint packed on the fins, and it looks much cleaner after a rinse. There's a faint warm, dusty smell in the room but no strong burning smell and no scorching that I've seen. I should say I often run the dryer while I'm out at work, if that matters.

The packed fluff on both the door filter and condenser is a strong explanation for the slow drying and very hot top: the dryer could not move enough air through itself. The faint warm dusty smell may be leftover lint warming up, but it should not become a strong burning smell. Let the rinsed condenser drain fully before refitting it, then do one short, supervised test only with a small-to-normal, well-spun load on a normal heat programme. Please do not run it while you are out until this has proved normal again; a dryer with a recent airflow blockage needs to be observed. 1. After 10–15 minutes, check whether the laundry is becoming warm and whether the smell remains faint or disappears. That supports the blockage having been the cause.
2. Stop immediately, unplug it and arrange an engineer if the smell strengthens, there is smoke, scorching, the dryer cuts out, or the casing becomes excessively hot again. With the filters now clear, that would point more towards lint further inside, a blower-fan issue, or temperature-control/overheat-protection parts rather than something to replace blindly. Clean the door filter after every load, and the condenser routinely, to prevent a repeat.
[Safety panel] Overheating can be a fire risk. Clean the lint filter and make sure the airflow/vent isn't blocked, and don't leave the dryer running unattended. If it smells of burning, stop using it and unplug it.

candidates: Restricted airflow from lint filter, condenser or vent path (high)
Overloading, very wet laundry or an unsuitable programme (medium)
Thermostat/overheat protection or fan fault after airflow checks (low)

reading.symptom: taking a long time to dry; top gets really hot

plan: Already given by the customer, never ask for it again: make Hotpoint; model TCM580GUK.
The fault they reported is: "taking a long time to dry; top gets really hot". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the safe checks that best tell those causes apart (most useful and simplest first, usually two to four), each with why it helps and what each result would mean; or, if one question would settle it sooner, ask that. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.

candidates: Restricted airflow from the heavily blocked fluff filter and condenser (high)
Residual lint in the air path or blower fan area (medium)
Thermostat or thermal cut-out problem after overheating (low)
